findings.consequence: If a pallet jams at the conveyor entry photo-eye, the jam condition will not be detected. The conveyor motor will continue running against the stalled pallet, risking motor burnout, conveyor belt damage, or pack enclosure damage.
findings.evidence: Lint reports input X11 (PE-1002) is unused. The parameter sheet specifies jam_time of 5.0 s on timer T10. Cause-and-effect matrix item CE-ST10-03 requires stopping conveyor motor Y10 and raising a jam alarm if PE-1002 is blocked for more than 5.0 s while running. In the program, M190 is reset in R2 by X1 and checked in R3 to stop Y10, but M190 is never set anywhere, and neither X11 nor T10 appears in the program.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the jam detection timer and latching rung before R2: LD Y10; AND X11; OUT T10 K50; LD T10; SET M190. This ensures M190 latches when the eye is blocked for 5.0 s while running, tripping M199 and stopping Y10 until reset by PB-0002 (X1).
findings.title: Conveyor Entry Jam Detection Logic Completely Missing

findings.consequence: If the conveyor motor thermal overload trips (X13 opens) and subsequently self-resets after cooling down, M191 will drop to 0 and M199 will clear. Because SS-0003 auto mode (X2) remains active, conveyor motor Y10 will restart automatically without operator intervention or fault reset, posing an unexpected restart hazard to personnel inspecting or clearing the conveyor.
findings.evidence: In R1, M191 is driven directly with OUT from LDI X13. In R2, fault reset pushbutton X1 only resets M190 and does not reset M191. Narrative §4.8 specifies that latched alarms clear with fault reset once their cause has cleared.
findings.proposed_fix: Latch the motor overload alarm using SET M191 on LDI X13 in R1, and add RST M191 to R2 when fault reset pushbutton X1 is pressed.
findings.title: Motor Overload Alarm is Non-Latched Causing Automatic Restart Hazard

findings.consequence: If the line controller issues release request RQ-1005 while the station is in manual mode, faulted, or in an emergency stop, the mechanical stopper drops for 2.0 s. This can cause uncommanded pallet movement into downstream stations or create pinch/crush hazards during maintenance or fault recovery.
findings.evidence: In R6, LDP X14 directly sets stopper release solenoid Y11 without checking whether auto mode is active (X2), E-stop is healthy (X0), or ST10 is faulted (M199). Additionally, if E-stop trips while Y11 is energized, Y11 remains held until timer T11 expires.
findings.proposed_fix: Interlock R6 with auto mode, E-stop healthy, and no fault: LD X2; AND X0; ANI M199; ANDP X14; SET Y11. Additionally, ensure Y11 is immediately reset if E-stop is lost: LDI X0; RST Y11.
findings.title: Stopper Release Solenoid Lacks Auto Mode, E-Stop, and Fault Interlocks

data.summary: The ST10 conveyor program exhibits three significant issues: (1) jam detection logic (entry photo-eye X11, timer T10, and latching of M190) is entirely missing despite being required by CE-ST10-03 and referenced in R2/R3; (2) motor overload alarm M191 is unlatched, allowing the conveyor to restart automatically upon thermal overload reset; and (3) stopper release solenoid Y11 operates unconditionally on line controller request without verifying Auto mode, E-stop healthy, or station fault status.
